targets.authors: Levinson DB, Stoll EL, Kindy SD, Merry HL, Davidson RJ.
targets.title: A mind you can count on: validating breath counting as a behavioral measure of mindfulness.
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted a study to replicate and extend the results of Levinson et al. (2014), who validated a breath-counting task as an objective measure of trait mindfulness.
targets.outcome_quote: To summarize the findings we replicated the following: BCT performance showed good test-retest reliability, showed a trend correlation with subjectively measured mindfulness (MAAS scores), and a significant correlation with performance on a test of sustained attention.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The authors explicitly summarize the tested findings as replicated. The weaker mindfulness correlation is treated as supporting the same association and is not an author-framed failure.

reasoning: A new Asian undergraduate sample retests the reliability and validity findings from Levinson et al. The other studies provide background or measurement instruments. No original-data reanalysis is reported.
